rv.q: At root, such solo endeavours evince the potency of storytelling and there were few better storytellers than Charles Dickens, who brought his own page-turners to the stage in rapturously received renditions.
Now we find Izzard doing a spellbinding solo turn in Charles Dickens's saga of self-discovery, Great Expectations.
It is a moot point whether this show confirms Izzard's credentials as a serious dramatic actor but what she certainly proves here is her unparalleled, really rather sublime, storytelling chops.
Izzard does herself, and Dickens, proud.
Eddie Izzard's solo offering is a welcome but surprisingly staid addition to the canon, offering a loving, detailed take on Dickens's most lovable novel.

Of course, there is the impressive feat of memory. This is a two-plus-hour monologue that romps through the book – minus straggling characters like Orlick and a couple of Pockets – and Izzard remains onstage throughout, tottering in knee-length lace-ups, her outfit black and white and frilly, her arms doing a great deal of characterisation.
If you're a neutral, as I am, be warned that it's an evening which has its longueurs as well as its charms.
Izzard's charm just about gets this thin piece over the line, but she only briefly captures the bittersweet pathos of Dickens's story at the very end.
This is very special, and surely a must-see for Eddie Izzard fans and Charles Dickens enthusiasts.

Charles Dickens was the great storyteller of his time, his live readings provoking tears of sadness in his audience. Eddie Izzard is one of the great storytellers of our time, tears of laughter her currency, her stand-up shows selling out as once did Dickens’ personal appearances.
